subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add `models status --probe --all` as the canonical all-configured-model health probe, and how should it scope live requests, JSON fields, timeout/concurrency, rate-limit handling, and overlap with fallback-chain or staged-migration diagnostics?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding an opt-in live probe across configured models changes CLI/provider diagnostics behavior and overlaps adjacent open product requests, so automation should not choose the permanent contract alone.

options.title: Define and implement status probe all
options.body: Use the existing `models status --probe` surface, add `--all`, and specify the live-request, JSON, docs, and proof contract before implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader migration/fallback UX
options.body: Keep this issue open as part of a larger model-safety workflow that also owns fallback-chain testing and staged promotion/rollback.

options.title: Defer core command surface
options.body: Leave manual `infer model run` or external monitoring as the workaround until maintainers want a broader core diagnostics contract.

recommendation.title: Define and implement status probe all
recommendation.body: Use the existing `models status --probe` surface, add `--all`, and specify the live-request, JSON, docs, and proof contract before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history in the model status/probe files and prior ClawSweeper issue guidance routes similar model-diagnostics product choices through this area.
